analysis.investment_thesis: Firstsource is a steady BPO operator with consistent OCF, but its D/E of 0.54 breaches my hard limit, and a BPO business facing AI-driven automation risk is not the kind of predictable, consumer-facing compounder I seek. Declining FCF (₹806 Cr in FY21 → ₹477 Cr in FY25) while debt nearly doubled to ₹2,369 Cr signals capital allocation moving in the wrong direction.
key_strengths: Consistent OCF generation — positive all 5 years, steady 10.6% revenue CAGR over 9 years
Operating margins held at ~12%, with operating income CAGR of 13.4% outpacing revenue growth
RPSG Group parentage provides institutional credibility and client access in global BPO markets
key_risks: Debt/Equity at 0.54 is a hard no — finance costs grew 13.1% CAGR, faster than revenue, consuming profit
Structural disruption risk: GenAI directly threatens BPO workloads in claims, collections, and customer service — the company's core
FCF deteriorating sharply (₹806 Cr FY21 → ₹477 Cr FY25) while cash is nearly exhausted at just ₹13 Cr — a balance sheet warning sign
red_flags: D/E of 0.54 breaches my absolute limit of 0.3 — borrowings jumped from ₹1,526 Cr to ₹2,369 Cr in a single year (FY25)
Cash position collapsed from ₹138 Cr (FY23) to ₹13 Cr (FY25) — dangerous near-zero liquidity
FCF yield of ~2.9% (₹477 Cr on ₹16,539 Cr mcap) is well below my 5% threshold
Promoter holding at 53.66% is below my 55% floor — mild but noted
P/E at 24x is above my 20x ceiling for quality businesses; BPO does not command a premium in my book
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Firstsource is a decent-quality IT services business — not a poor business, but not one I would own. It sits entirely outside my circle of competence. I built DMart by understanding shelves, suppliers, and housewives. BPO economics — currency risk on GBP/USD revenues, client concentration in US healthcare and UK banking, offshore wage inflation — are not businesses I can evaluate with conviction. When I cannot understand the durability of a business model deeply, I simply do not invest, regardless of the numbers.

The numbers here further reinforce caution. Debt has risen sharply — borrowings up 55% in FY25 alone, likely acquisition-driven given the ₹744 Cr investing outflow and total assets jumping ₹2,400 Cr in one year. Finance costs at ₹184 Cr in FY25 are eating 31% of net profit. ROE of 15% is at the low end of acceptability, and net profit CAGR of just 9.6% over 9 years means shareholders have compounded slower than the underlying business. The AI disruption risk to BPO is existential in ways that disruption to a grocery retailer is not — I can adapt shelf space; a BPO cannot easily re-skill thousands of agents overnight.
